sections.brief: Why and how Constantine summoned Nicaea (Arius vs Alexander from c.318; Constantine's 'idle question' letter; imperial post), who came (250-300 bishops, 318 traditional, 200-220 names on lists; five Western bishops, Rome by two presbyters; Persian and Scythian bishops; no Ethiopian bishop yet; Novatian Acesius invited; '1,800 invited' unsourced), Constantine's entrance and low gold chair, Hosius presiding, emperor not voting. Figures: stats

Arius's teaching; the 325 creed and anathemas; homoousios urged by Constantine per Eusebius of Caesarea's letter, earlier Gnostic use (Basilides, Ptolemy) and Antioch 268 condemnation; refusers (synodal letter's two vs Socrates' five), exiles to Illyria, Eusebius of Nicomedia and Theognis; Constantine's order to burn Arius's books (death for concealment); Easter and Constantine's anti-Jewish letter with Nostra Aetate 4; Melitians; canons 6, 7, 8, 19, 20; aftermath to Constantinople 381. Figures: flow (definition and enforcement); time (325-381)

the platform's 'Constantine, Paul, council decided Christianity' tested part by part; myths: canon/altar (Synodicon Vetus c.887-920, Pappus 1601, Voltaire), 'voted Jesus divine' (Da Vinci Code; Pliny c.111-113, Ignatius), burned gospels (only Arius's books; separate edict vs Valentinians etc. on meetings), reincarnation (553 anathemas against Origen), excluded Ethiopian/Gnostic bishops, creed today = 381 form + Filioque. Figures: compare (told vs record)
